notes: §1985:IX.2.7.2 prints RECORD KEY IS data-name-1, with RECORD the one underlined word. recordKeyClause requires RECORD, takes KEY and IS as optional words and one data-name operand; BindFileControl captures its base word and qualifiers through ClauseDataName (a subscripted or reference-modified operand is refused, COBOL2024); the 2023 alternative record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS data-name-2 is refused at 85 by VisitRecordKeySourcePhrase (COBOL0900), and a second RECORD KEY clause by ScreenClauseRepetition (COBOL2423). Probed at 85: RECORD KEY IS K1, RECORD KEY K1 and RECORD K1 OF R1 compile and run; KEY IS K1 without RECORD, a missing operand, a literal operand, a second data-name, WITH DUPLICATES after the key and K1 (1:2) are refused. The witness declares RECORD KEY IS IX-KEY, writes one record and reads it back at random by that key.

next.reason: 1985: "RECORD KEY IS data-name-1"; 2023: "RECORD KEY IS { data-name-1 | record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } … }". 2023 keeps the data-name-1 form but adds a split-key alternative (record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS data-name-2 …), so the format accepts a case 1985 did not.
